program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s binding is ambiguous and appears to identify the wrong object: the source shows a small rectangular DVD case near the center, while the edited image shows two white discs—one near center-left and one beside the dark object at right. The traces consistently call a white disc the DVD and mark the edit complete, but do not establish which disc corresponds to the source DVD or whether the original target was transformed versus replaced/duplicated. Refine the binding to anchor the target to its source location and distinctive case/disc context, and make the criterion compare that same object across source and edited images, distinguishing complete color change from partial change, absence, or insufficient identity evidence. Do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as independent confirmation of target identity; the disagreement is visual/semantic, not a transport or dependency failure.
